reason: Candidate C4 is the strongest hypothesis because it addresses the specific problem of room-temperature brittleness in refractory multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) with a highly concrete and specific intervention: a stepwise thermo-mechanical route (hot rolling, cold rolling, short annealing, aging) designed to create a dual-phase coherent precipitate structure (lamellar δ and spheroidal γ″). Unlike C1 and C3, which are vague about the specific precipitate types or rely on generic 'SCCP' terminology without structural detail, C4 specifies the crystal structures (D0a, D022) and morphologies. Unlike C2 and C6, which focus on severe plastic deformation (SPD) and nanograins (a mechanism more typical of FCC alloys or general strengthening), C4 targets the specific challenge of refractory BC
